name: seq_reg_pair
desc: Two ADD Rn,Dn back to back (no branch/marker between). MC68030UM.pdf 11-40/41: ADD Rn,Dn NCC=2(0/1/0) each. Isolated instr1 measures this RTL's own already-documented register-only dispatch floor (~3 clocks); instr2's own incremental cost (real sequential flow, benefiting from the IFU's own EX/WB-independent continuous prefetch) is expected to be dramatically smaller.

name: seq_extcount_pair
desc: Two ADDI.L #imm,Dn back to back. MC68030UM.pdf 11-40/42: ADDI #(data),Dn NCC=2(0/1/0) + FIEA(#imm.L,Dn)=2(0/1/0) = 4 each. Each instruction is ext_count==2 (needs a genuine second IFU fetch when the queue starts empty, Phase 165). Isolated instr1 measures the already-documented +4 gap; instr2's own incremental cost is expected to shrink substantially.

name: seq_rmw_pair
desc: Two NEG.L (An) at different addresses, back to back. MC68030UM.pdf 11-43/44: NEG Mem NCC=4(0/1/1) + fea((An))=3(1/0/0) = 7 each. Isolated instr1 measures the already-documented RMW-to-memory dispatch-floor +4 gap; instr2's own incremental cost is expected to improve only partially (real bus-arbitration contention -- a single physical bus can't serve two masters at once -- unlike the register-only/ext_count==2 clusters' own near-complete closure).

name: seq_mixed3
desc: A heterogeneous 3-instruction sequence: ADD Rn,Dn (NCC=2), NEG.L (An) (NCC=7), ADD Rn,Dn (NCC=2) -- the first test of a realistic mixed sequence rather than two copies of the same instruction, checking whether the overlap benefit generalizes across instruction-class boundaries.

name: seq_branch_pair
desc: ADD Rn,Dn (whose own real result sets Z=1) immediately followed by a taken BEQ.W depending on that result -- not isolated setup code. MC68030UM.pdf 11-48: Bcc (Taken) NCC=8(0/2/0). Checks whether the branch-redirect finding (pc_wr_en fires the same cycle as instr_ack, combinationally, confirmed via direct trace) holds when something real precedes the branch.
